content.title: Washington DC Cherry Blossom Watch Update: March 20, 2026
content.text: The cherry blossoms aren’t flowering yet, but there’s plenty of pink and white poking through when you look at them up close. And the saucer magnolias are still in the process of fully opening. Now that we’ve gotten through that stretch of unsettled weather, it should be clear sailing into the bloom. The cherry buds are progressing well, and you can see plenty of white and pink coming through now. There’s not much to see this weekend, but with a few quite warm days coming up, there should be plenty of flowers to see as we get deeper into next week. Next weekend (March 28-29) is shaping up to be a good cherry blossom viewing weekend, so expect crowds. But for now, it’s still very quiet. How it Looks at the Tidal Basin This Morning It’s still very quiet. There’s a small handful of early bloomers scattered around, but the vast majority of the trees haven’t started blooming yet. We have a few warm days coming up that will speed things along. But that will be followed, starting around the middle of the week, by cooler temperatures to slow down the pace to slow and steady. Photo by David Coleman / Cherry Blossom Watch Saucer Magnolias The saucer magnolias at the Enid A. Haupt Garden are still starting to bloom. There are still plenty yet to fully open, and over the next few warmer days, more will come out. When you look at them up close, you can see definite signs of the damage from the storms and cold earlier in the week. Those flowers that were already open were the most vulnerable, and many of them were damaged. Those that were still closed fared much better, but even on those, many of them show at least some brown damage. Witches’ Brooms Look closely at the tree branches; if you see a dense, tangled ball of twigs that looks like a bird's nest, it's likely a "Witch's Broom." It’s a genetic mutation or fungal reaction, not a nest. Coming into town for the cherry blossoms? Here are some planning resources I’ve put together to help you make the most of your visit. Where to Stay If you’re coming from out of town, I’ve put together some ideas on where to stay for the cherry blossoms. These are some of the most convenient to the Tidal Basin.
